newsitem.title: UK: BOC, Courtaulds down ahead of results.
newsitem.headline: BOC, Courtaulds down ahead of results.

text.p: Shares in BOC Group Plc and Courtaulds Plc dropped on Monday amid jitters over results later this week, traders said.
BOC touched their lowest level since October 1995 ahead of full-year results tomorrow while Courtaulds fell to a four-month low ahead of first-half results on Wednesday.

BOC was down 13p at 824 by 0939 GMT, with tomorrow's full-year profits expected to be squeezed by sterling strength as well as already-flagged problems affecting its vacuum and health businesses. Last week SBC Warburg cut its forecast for pretax profit at the group to 421 million stg from 438 million to reflect tough trading in its vacuum and anaesthetics businesses.

Analysts expect BOC to post pre-tax profits of between 421 million stg and 445 million compared with 402 million a year before, though the strength of sterling could eat into the value of the company's overseas earnings.
At Courtaulds, analysts expect pretax profit of between 65.0 million stg and 70.0 million, compared with 67.8 million a year before.

The stock has been hit in recent weeks by a series of downgrades from major brokerages. Most recently ABN AMRO Hoare Govett cut its estimate for pretax in fiscal 1997 by a fifth because of pressure on its key textiles business.

Traders said BOC and Courtaulds shares were marked lower amid worries about their forthcoming results. "It is just a bit of nervousness ahead of the figures," said a market-maker at one leading brokerage.
Another said recent results from Imperial Chemical Industries Plc, showing tumbling third-quarter profits, continued to cast a shadow over the rest of the disparate chemical sector.
"People won't be committing new money because they know how tricky a time it has been following the ICI statement," the second trader said.
ICI shares were down 3-1/2p at 764 -- not far short of their intraday low for the year of 737p set July 30.
